text.full: Built vision systems turning raw camera feeds into perception-ready frames across 3 workstreams: camera ISP, super-resolution, and image restoration under real-world blur.

Reproduced a published UNet super-resolution model in PyTorch from broken author code, recovering its undocumented evaluation protocol and training 12 models across 3 scales, 2 datasets, and 2 losses, matching reported results at 8x and landing within 0.78 dB at 2x and 4x.

Diagnosed a robustness gap where fixed-blur models lost most PSNR gains under unseen blur, then added randomised-blur training and fine-tuning to recover up to 0.7 dB across 3 real-world blur types: lens, out-of-focus, and resampling.

Authored and presented a super-resolution literature review spanning multi-image, video, and single-image methods, organised around camera information loss and recovery through calibration, extra frames, or learned priors, comparing 4 model families on fidelity and hallucination risk.

Deployed 3 trained models as a public web app: a one-click Flask inference API on a Colab T4 GPU loading weights from a GitHub release, a secure tunnel on a reserved domain, and a hosted front end for image upload, scale selection, and download.
